intro.narrative: One paragraph shown to the group that introduces the case. This is the PRIMARY thing all participants read to set the scene.
intro.company_info: Optional static background about the organization.

attack_chain.name: How they got in
attack_chain.symptom: What the group observes that hints at this stage. Plain language, executive-friendly — no technical jargon.

attack_chain.name: How it spread
attack_chain.symptom: What the group observes as the attack spreads.

attack_chain.name: What they took
attack_chain.symptom: What the group observes as the attack reaches its goal.

dm_brief.situation: Full background the DM uses to adjudicate. Describe the world, the current problem, and what is at stake.
dm_brief.stakes: What is lost if the group fails.
pressure_points: (Optional, backward-compat) An event the DM may inject if the group stalls.
Prefer the top-level 'events' array below for conditional, once-per-session events.
rules_of_play: Never propose actions or present a menu of choices; react only to what the group does.
Only metrics the scenario tracks may change; keep values between 0 and 100.
Reveal an attack-chain stage when the group's investigation plausibly uncovers it; mark it contained when the group neutralizes it.
Enforce detection as a resource: the group cannot do everything at once, and activating monitoring costs budget.

events.text: An event that fires if the group stalls for 2 turns.
An event that fires when public_trust drops to 40 or below (the team is failing).

beats.name: Step 1 — <name the first stage of the story>
beats.narrative: <What the group faces in this step and what it takes to resolve it. The DM advances to the next beat when the group closes this one out.>

beats.name: Step 2 — <next stage>
beats.narrative: <What the group faces now. If Step 1 went well this is softer; if it went poorly this is worse.>

goal.description: OPTIONAL goal (win condition). Use it for IT/kill-chain exercises where there is a concrete objective to achieve (hit all win_conditions, or contain all attack-chain stages). OMIT goal for executive/fallout exercises (e.g. a data leak) where there is no "win" — the session then runs to a lose condition or timeout and the report is the debrief. When ALL win_conditions are met simultaneously, the scenario ends in success.
goal.ending: Crisis resolved: the attack chain is contained and trust restored. The exercise concludes.

end_conditions.ending: The collapse: the story ends badly. Replace this with a vivid, scenario-specific narration of the organization losing the confidence of the people it serves, the regulator escalating, and the board losing faith in the response. The exercise concludes as a loss.
Time ran out on the scheduled exercise.

report.audit_note: Generated automatically at session end or timeout.
